NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 7 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 25 · 10 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 25, 12:04 PM ET

Brock Bowers is the top-projected tight end on the Week 7 DraftKings main slate at 17.3 DraftKings points for $7,700, against the Rams. George Kittle (17.1, $5,700) and Trey McBride (15.8, $7,400) are next.

Cade Otton returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 3.38 projected points per $1,000 at $3,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 25, 12:04 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 7

Brock Bowers, LV vs LAR ($7,700)

Brock Bowers carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 17.3 DraftKings points at $7,700. That is 0.2 points clear of George Kittle. The model gives him 8.8 targets on 34.1 routes. The salary works out to 2.25 projected points per $1,000, 11th of 14 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 17.2 points with a simulated floor of 4.0 and a ceiling of 42.5, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 3.5-point underdog at home against the Rams, with an implied team total of 22.5 in a game totaled at 48.5.

George Kittle, SF at ATL ($5,700)

George Kittle projects 2nd at the position with 17.1 DraftKings points at $5,700. The model gives him 7.0 targets on 22.7 routes. The salary works out to 3.00 projected points per $1,000, 2nd of 14 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Kittle averaged 17.1 points with a simulated floor of 3.7 and a ceiling of 43.4, and he holds 23% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 2.5-point favorite on the road against Atlanta, with an implied team total of 26.5 in a game totaled at 50.5.

Value: Cade Otton, TB at CAR ($3,100)

Cade Otton projects for 10.5 DraftKings points at $3,100, which works out to 3.38 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 14 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 6.4 targets on 30.6 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Otton averaged 10.4 points with a simulated floor of 0.1 and a ceiling of 32.7, and he holds 19% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Tampa Bay is a 3-point underdog on the road against Carolina, with an implied team total of 20.75 in a game totaled at 44.5.
